Third-party software bundled with ValeLoot
==========================================

BepInEx 6 (IL2CPP), bleeding-edge build be.785
----------------------------------------------

The "with BepInEx" download of ValeLoot contains BepInEx so that installing is one unzip instead of
"first go and find the right BepInEx build". That matters more than convenience: BepInEx 5 and the stable
6 release do NOT load plugins into an IL2CPP game, and the download page does not make that obvious, so
the commonest way to fail at installing this mod was picking the wrong one. Bundling removes that choice.

  Project:   BepInEx
  Version:   6.0.0-be.785  (IL2CPP, win-x64)
  Source:    https://github.com/BepInEx/BepInEx
  Build:     https://builds.bepinex.dev/projects/bepinex_be  (build 785)
  Licence:   GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1 — see BepInEx-LICENSE.txt beside this file

BepInEx is included **unmodified**, exactly as published by its authors. It is not a part of ValeLoot and
ValeLoot claims no copyright in it. If you already have BepInEx 6 IL2CPP installed, take the plain
`ValeLoot-<version>.zip` instead — it contains only the plugin.

Under the LGPL you are entitled to the source of the bundled library and to replace it with your own
build: the source is at the URL above, and BepInEx is loaded dynamically from `BepInEx/core/`, so
replacing those files with another 6.x IL2CPP build is supported and does not require rebuilding ValeLoot.

ValeLoot itself is a separate work that uses BepInEx's published plugin API. Its own licence and terms
are in its README.

Doorstop
--------

The BepInEx distribution embeds Unity Doorstop (`winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`), which is how the
runtime is loaded before the game starts. It ships under BepInEx's own distribution and carries its own
notices inside that archive; see https://github.com/NeighTools/UnityDoorstop.

NOTICES
-------

Everything in this download that is not listed above is ValeLoot's own work, under the MIT licence in
the LICENSE file of https://github.com/bjb2/valeloot.

That includes the loot-filter parser compiled into the rule editor page. The page carries it as
ordinary inlined JavaScript rather than loading it from anywhere, so the editor works offline; it is
MIT code from this project, not a third-party library, and no other licence applies to it.
